key_question_answer: No. A reviewer would not see the AURA-converted source as substantially the same architecture as the existing upstream lpass-va-macro.c. They would see partial alignment: the conversion uses local CDC_VA registers, devm_snd_soc_register_component, lpass_macro_pds_init/exit, runtime PM callbacks, and direct clock APIs. However, the remaining regmap ownership model, compatible/SoC-data model, fsgen clock-provider model, DAPM/control topology, and helper structure are still materially different from upstream.

summary_metrics.verdict_basis: Partial alignment: runtime PM pattern and includes are close, but exact line similarity is low and major probe/regmap/fsgen/DAPM architecture deltas remain.

top_10_largest_remaining_differences.reason: Largest delta contains upstream fsgen clock-provider, SoC-compatible data model, probe/remove structure, runtime tail, and of_device_id architecture.
Private data and helper model differ: upstream va_macro owns regmap/data/clk_hw state while converted source retains downstream-derived private state.
Clock and mclk helper paths differ structurally; converted source uses parent regmap and downstream user-counting while upstream uses va->regmap and compact fsgen/mclk helpers.
Converted TX enable path retains downstream mute/HPF/decimator sequencing that upstream does not implement in this form.
Converted DAPM routes retain downstream SoundWire/SMIC route topology that differs from upstream route model.
